You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed along its front closure?
node.criteria: Pass only if the visible front closure shows the jacket fully closed, with the front panels meeting and no visible opening remaining along the closure. Fail if visible evidence shows an open gap or that the jacket is only partly closed. Unknown if the closure line or whether the panels meet cannot be determined because it is obscured by the woman's pose, draped fabric, folds, or insufficient image detail.
node.binding: Judge the woman's jacket in the edited image against the requested fully closed state. Assess the actual front closure and whether the panels meet; do not infer an open closure solely from a hanging or separated-looking panel when the closure is obscured.

node_traces.evidence: In the edited image, the woman is turned sideways and the jacket front is obscured by her pose and a hanging, draped panel. The front closure and whether the panels meet cannot be determined.

response.content: {"text":"The node is already correctly bound to the requested jacket closure, and its uncertainty is grounded in the edited image: the woman is turned sideways and the front is hidden by the draped panel, so closure cannot be verified. Do not force a “yes” from the reference label or treat the hanging panel alone as proof of an open closure. The trace is valid and queried, with no transport, schema, or dependency failure; the zero coverage reflects insufficient visual evidence, not a failed execution. For future robustness, keep the criterion focused on observable evidence of whether the front panels meet, and distinguish a visible closed closure, a visible opening, and an obscured/indeterminate closure. The source image shows a different pose and cannot establish the edited image’s closure state. Investigate whether the edit or view exposes the closure sufficiently; low confidence or repeated variation would not itself prove the requested change is absent."}
